status: FROZEN architecture, fresh n=8 validation set - see artifacts/v2/phase8_frozen_config.json and phase8_validation_manifest.json

expected_vs_actual_stop_reason_match.VAL-D-duplicate-only-followup: partial - gap resolved before the forced duplicate round could execute (see caveat)

match_rate_exact: 4/8 exact match; 4/8 differ in SPECIFIC predicted stop reason but all 8/8 terminated safely/boundedly with zero fabrication
disclosed_findings: VAL-C: a genuine Claim Support Precision regression (1.0 -> 0.667) occurred after a productive completeness-improving follow-up introduced a new, only-partially-supported claim. The loop itself correctly detected this (gap_type=weakly_supported_fact persisted) and did NOT report sufficient_evidence - it stopped via no_productive_action because no further real evidence was available in this simulation to resolve it. This is disclosed, not hidden: research_stop_reason and research_gaps on the final state accurately reflect the unresolved issue.

Known limitation (validation-discovered): the final rendered GroundedAnswer text is not automatically caveated/modified when the loop stops for a reason other than sufficient_evidence (e.g. no_productive_action with a residual weakly_supported_fact gap). This is a pre-existing Phase-6 rendering boundary, not something Phase 8 makes worse - Phase 8 is a net improvement here since it is the first component able to DETECT and RECORD this condition at all - but it is not yet wired to suppress/caveat the specific weak claim in the user-facing text. Recommended as explicit follow-up work, not fixed here (post-freeze, no tuning).

VAL-F: MAX_REPEATED_ACTION (never retry an identical action) took precedence over MAX_CONSECUTIVE_TOOL_FAILURE_ROUNDS in this case, since the single available gap had only one candidate action, which failed once and could never be retried - so the loop correctly reached no_productive_action rather than tool_failure_limit. Both are valid, safe, bounded terminal states; this reveals a real interaction between two independent bounds, not a defect.

VAL-D: the gap resolved after one productive follow-up round before the pre-registered forced duplicate round could execute (the loop correctly stopped rather than continuing unnecessarily) - the duplicate-handling scenario itself was NOT exercised end-to-end in this specific validation run as originally designed; it remains covered by the dedicated offline integration test test_productive_followup_adds_new_evidence_and_dedupes_on_rediscovery.

VAL-H: the predeclared persistently-recurring gap did not materialize live (zero gaps were detected from the single initial pubmed record, given live NLU/judge behavior) - budget_exhausted was not exercised in this validation run; it remains covered by the dedicated offline test test_decide_stop_never_infinite_for_a_persistently_unresolved_gap and test_decide_stop_budget_exhausted_on_iteration_limit/test_decide_stop_budget_exhausted_on_tool_call_limit.
